quotes.text: This creates a fundamental problem, hourly consulting incentivizes you to sell more hours. It does not incentivize you to create lasting value or reduce client dependency.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core incentive problem of hourly consulting in two sentences.

quotes.text: The gap is not technical. It is not a skills deficit. It is architectural entropy. It is the inevitable decay of governance when intent is not enforced by design.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines the governance gap that all five business models exploit.

quotes.text: Identity is now the only perimeter that matters. The network perimeter is dead. VPN is dead. The traditional security model built on firewalls and network segmentation does not function when users work anywhere.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for identity-first security behind the Entra-first boutique model.

quotes.text: The dashboard is not the product. The dashboard is a display mechanism. The actual product is the decision that gets made based on the data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shifts the value of BI from reporting to automated decisions.

quotes.text: Consultants execute tasks. Architects make decisions about system behavior and governance that produce measurable results. One is replaceable. The other is defensible.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sharp distinction between consultant and architect roles.

chapters.title: Why the hourly consulting model is dying
Model 5: Industry tenant in a box
Pricing, sales motion, traps and the 12-month roadmap

takeaways: Hourly Microsoft 365 consulting is turning into a commodity; the growing gap between what Microsoft ships and what organizations can govern is where specialized, outcome-based practices earn premium prices.

The five models are an agentic workflow factory, an Entra-first security boutique, governance as a service, a decision engine architect and an industry tenant in a box, each combining a build phase with recurring revenue.
Success depends on deep specialization in one model and vertical, not underpricing the build phase, active customer success and a real shift from selling hours to owning outcomes.
hook: Microsoft 365 implementation work is becoming a commodity, and hourly rates keep falling. This episode is for consultants, architects and IT professionals who want to build a scalable Microsoft 365 business. You will learn five outcome-based models across AI agents, Entra security, governance, decision automation and productized tenants, with the pricing and positioning behind each.
